record.original_question: For each positive integer n, determine C(n), the number of Costas arrays of order n. In particular, do Costas arrays exist for every order n > 0, and if not, which positive integers n satisfy C(n) = 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Determine the number C(n) of Costas arrays of order n ∈ N* . In particular, is C(n) > 0 for all n > 0? If not, determine the set X = {n ∈ N* : C(n) = 0}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and one dot in each column (i.e., a permutation matrix of size n×n) such that all the displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are distinct. Equivalently, a permutation f: {1,…,n} → {1,…,n} is a Costas permutation if for every integers i, j, k with 1 ≤ i, j, j+k ≤ n and k ≠ 0, the equality f(i+k) − f(i) = f(j+k) − f(j) implies i = j. Let C(n) denote the number of Costas arrays of order n.

(a) For every positive integer n, determine the value of C(n).

(b) Decide whether C(n) > 0 holds for every positive integer n; if not, determine explicitly the set X = { n ∈ ℤ_{>0} : C(n) = 0 } of orders for which no Costas array exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. No closed-form expression for C(n) is known, and the existence question is famously unresolved: as of recent enumeration efforts (covering orders up to roughly 29 exhaustively, with partial searches extending much further), it is still unknown whether Costas arrays exist for order n = 32 and n = 33, the smallest orders where existence has not been decided. Asymptotic gaps between known upper and lower bounds for C(n) also remain open.

status_evidence.title: Costas array - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether Costas arrays exist for all orders; the smallest orders for which no Costas array is currently known are 32 and 33.

status_evidence.title: Costas arrays and enumeration to order 1030
status_evidence.snippet: Enumeration databases of Costas arrays to order 1030 are available; lists are likely near complete but additional arrays of order > 29 may exist.
status_evidence.claim: Full enumeration is not complete beyond order 29.

status_evidence.title: The enumeration of Costas arrays of order 28
status_evidence.snippet: Exhaustive enumeration through order 29 has been completed; further orders remain open.
status_evidence.claim: C(n) is exactly known only for small n.
